turns.text: I use nitroglycerin spray for angina a couple of times a week, and I'm starting a new relationship. I'm worried about sex and my heart — how should I approach this safely?
Why does angina make physical exertion risky, and how much exertion is sex actually, compared with, say, climbing stairs?
What warning signs during exertion should I take seriously, and what should I do if I get them?
If I raised this with my cardiologist, what would they want to know and what tests might they suggest?
What do cardiac rehab nurses usually tell people about intimacy after a heart diagnosis?
A friend in the same situation said pacing and choosing the time of day made a big difference. Is that true?
Someone else told me to keep the spray to hand and not be embarrassed about it. Is that reasonable?
I'm 62 and this is the first relationship since my wife died, and I'm nervous about all of it. How do I talk to her about my heart?
Is there anything about how I use the spray in a typical week that suggests my angina isn't as controlled as it should be?
Can you give me a plan — what to do this weekend, what to have on hand, warning signs, and the questions to bring to the cardiologist?
